editorial:
Imagine being a teenager in the early 2000s, raised in a strict Catholic school, and suddenly discovering your own body in the most awkward way possible. That is exactly where Alice finds herself in this funny and heartfelt coming-of-age story. After a random AOL chat turns unexpectedly sexual, Alice starts exploring herself and immediately feels crushed by guilt. The movie follows her as she tries to balance her faith, her curiosity, and the confusing messages adults keep sending her. It is a small, intimate film that feels honest and real, never mocking its characters but gently poking fun at the mixed signals of growing up.

The standout here is the lead performance, which carries the whole movie with charm and vulnerability. The pacing is relaxed and easy to follow, letting the awkward moments breathe without dragging. On the downside, some scenes feel a little repetitive, and the story stays small rather than building to big drama. Still, if you enjoy character-driven comedies with heart, this one is a treat.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Alice discovers that the priest leading her retreat is the same person behind the sexual AOL chat that started everything. This twist exposes the hypocrisy behind the strict rules she has been taught. Instead of feeling more guilt, Alice finally lets go of the shame. She returns home, tells her mom the retreat was fine, and quietly embraces her own body and choices. The movie ends on a hopeful note, showing Alice accepting herself without the heavy burden of sin.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories with humor and heart.
